controls.reason: Seven named quality dimensions can each be bound to an explicit metric, threshold, scope, and gate result in a versioned policy record.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a qualitative `looks good` gate, a dimension without a threshold, and a gate outside the assessed revision; measurability and binding checks reject each. Gate wisdom is not asserted.

controls.reason: The rule is a documentation requirement for eight explicit assumption topics, which current versioned sections or structured entries decide completely.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried omitting trust assumptions, recording dependencies without environment assumptions, and stale timing notes; exact topic and freshness checks fail each. Assumption truth is not claimed.

controls.reason: A temporary-code inventory cannot independently discover every experiment, bypass, shim, or migration, so unrecorded items evade owner and removal checks.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An emergency authorization bypass is hidden behind a feature flag and omitted from the register. Every registered temporary item has an owner and removal condition, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Which behavior is important and whether six contract sections fully specify it require semantic judgment; a record can omit important paths or contain placeholders.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A critical refund workflow is labelled unimportant, while another behavior has six fields containing `standard`. The schema passes although important behavior remains unspecified.

controls.reason: The proposal does not prove a complete input-boundary inventory or substantive behavior definitions for all nine edge classes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A batch-import endpoint is omitted and has undefined duplicate handling; listed APIs contain nine nonempty headings. The record passes while real input behavior remains undefined.

controls.reason: Operation scope is not independently complete, and generic field values do not define coherent semantics for interruption, timeout, retry, and recovery.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unlisted payout job has no cancellation behavior, while listed operations say `error` for every condition. Required fields pass but partial-completion behavior is not defined.

controls.reason: Applicability of six distributed guarantees varies by operation, and the acceptance record can omit operations or use undefined values without proving explicit requirements.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A message handler requiring idempotency is absent from the contract; all listed services have six fields. The proposal passes while an applicable idempotency requirement is missing.

controls.reason: Records cannot prove a complete business-rule inventory or detect semantically replicated rules hidden in code, configuration, database logic, and external services.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A discount rule is duplicated with different rounding in a database trigger omitted from the registry. All declared rules point to one source, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Production-semantic equivalence with assertions or diagnostics disabled is a whole-program behavioral claim that source syntax and finite fixtures cannot prove.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A diagnostic callback performs required cache invalidation only when enabled; fixtures never hit that path. Static checks pass while disabling diagnostics changes production results.

controls.reason: A shared change record cannot prove specification impact was completely identified or that implementation and specification remain semantically synchronized.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A configuration change alters retry semantics but is labelled implementation-only, so no spec change is joined. All declared spec changes share reviews while the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Identifying a design-principle violation and judging that its trade-off is safer or simpler require contextual design and risk judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A record calls global mutable state a DRY trade-off and says it is simpler. All fields pass although reviewers can reasonably find the design less safe and more complex.

controls.reason: Dependency records and declared interfaces cannot enumerate dynamic loading, reflection, environment lookup, database triggers, provider behavior, and hidden runtime coupling.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A module reads an undeclared environment variable and calls a provider through a generated client. Listed dependencies are explicit, so the record passes despite hidden dependencies.

controls.reason: A versioned formatter and style configuration can run read-only over the sealed source inventory, making consistency an exact zero-deviation gate.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an excluded source file, formatting under another config version, and an ignored violation; inventory, config digest, and formatter-result checks reject each. Review focus is rationale, not another condition.

controls.reason: Syntax cannot reliably distinguish commented-out code from examples or pseudocode, and whether an explanation is obsolete requires semantic and historical judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A stale comment describes behavior removed last year but contains no code tokens, while a valid documentation example resembles disabled code. A mechanical rule cannot classify both correctly.

controls.reason: A generated-file register cannot independently prove every generated file or section is included, so unmarked output can remain hidden.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A generated migration file is copied into source and omitted from the generation manifest. Every registered artifact has markers and a source link, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Detecting sentinel collisions requires complete semantic domain sets and every value flow; syntax and supplied contracts can omit valid runtime values.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Code uses zero as `not found`, while a new tenant legitimately has identifier zero outside the declared domain fixture. Static checks pass despite the collision.

controls.reason: A compatibility-policy record does not prove every parser actually preserves or rejects unknown fields on all paths and versions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: One legacy consumer silently drops unknown fields despite a record saying preserve; it is absent from the parser inventory. The structured contract passes while runtime behavior violates it.

controls.reason: Authoritative interface schemas can explicitly record defaults and separate omitted from supplied-default semantics wherever outcomes differ.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an implicit default, one representation for absent and explicit values despite differing behavior, and a stale schema; exact schema checks fail each.

controls.reason: Numeric fields in a contract do not prove limits are safe or enforced across every collection, recursive path, nested format, and graph traversal.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A parser declares depth 1000 as safe but exhausts its stack at 200, and an unlisted graph traversal has no limit. Record fields pass while the control is false.

controls.reason: The seven required error categories form a closed taxonomy schema, so exact distinct identifiers and definitions decide whether it is defined.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried merging transient and permanent failure, omitting programmer defect, and using duplicate identifiers; enum and distinctness checks reject each. Runtime classification accuracy is separate.

controls.reason: Typed error syntax does not prove callers can make safe decisions or that no call path parses human-readable messages.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unlisted client branches on `message.includes('denied')`, while declared callers use error codes. All inventoried types pass but a caller still makes unsafe text-based decisions.

controls.reason: Cleanup across all success, failure, cancellation, timeout, and abrupt-termination paths is a universal runtime property over incomplete resource and control-flow inventories.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An abrupt worker termination leaks a provider lease on a path the analyzer cannot model. Listed local resources have `finally` blocks, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Cancellation and deadline propagation through every transitive, dynamic, remote, queued, and callback dependency cannot be proven from a declared call graph.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A database job spawned through reflection drops the deadline but is absent from the graph. All declared calls pass tokens, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Product distinction and telemetry separation must hold across every cancellation path and requires semantic mapping of user intent, not only different error codes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A browser close is logged as failure and shown as an error on an unlisted flow. Declared cancellation cases use a separate code, so source checks pass.

controls.reason: Retry implementations and dependency guidance are not completely enumerable, and source patterns do not prove runtime backoff, jitter distribution, or dynamic server instructions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An SDK performs immediate hidden retries and ignores `Retry-After`; declared retry loops contain backoff calls. The source contract passes while amplification remains possible.

controls.reason: Preventing amplification, duplicate effects, and infinite retries is a distributed behavioral claim across callers, dependencies, concurrency, and side effects.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Two services each retry three times and multiply requests, although each local loop meets its bound. Static local checks pass while system-wide amplification occurs.

controls.reason: A state registry can omit stateful components, and field presence does not prove lifecycle, transition, persistence, and reset semantics are coherent or explicit.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A cached authorization state is absent from the registry; listed state rows contain generic `default` transitions. The schema passes while important state ownership remains unclear.

controls.reason: Whether a workflow is consequential or nontrivial requires contextual risk judgment, allowing applicable workflows to be excluded before the state-machine check.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A payout workflow is labelled simple and implemented with scattered booleans, while every declared consequential workflow has a state machine. The proposal passes.

controls.reason: A derived-state inventory cannot independently discover every cache, projection, denormalized field, index, and computed copy.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A database-maintained summary table is omitted and has no invalidation rule. Every registered derived state has all three sections, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Event-contract records can omit streams and handlers, and nonempty outcome fields need not define coherent behavior for all four timing anomalies.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A legacy consumer has no late-event behavior but is absent from the registry; listed contracts say `handle` without semantics. The proposal passes.

controls.reason: Persisted-state inventories can omit stores and versions, and a migration path can exist on paper without being controlled, executable, or complete.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A browser database is omitted and cannot migrate two old versions; registered schemas have version fields and nominal migration links. The proposal passes.

controls.reason: No structured record can prove it identifies every shared mutable resource across memory, files, databases, caches, providers, processes, and generated code.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A global cache mutated by a plugin is omitted from the resource inventory. Every declared resource has a concurrency model, so the universal claim passes falsely.

controls.reason: API and component inventories can omit runtime surfaces, and a thread-safety label does not prove that the documented classification is correct.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unlisted callback is concurrently invoked despite being unsafe; every registered API has a nonempty threading label. The record passes while documentation is incomplete or false.

controls.reason: Static limit syntax cannot enumerate all concurrency, queue, buffer, and fan-out mechanisms or prove limits hold after composition and dynamic configuration.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Two individually bounded fan-out stages multiply into unbounded work, while each declared local limit passes. A hidden in-memory queue also has no bound.

controls.reason: Nonempty trade-off and consequence sections do not establish that real consistency risks and user-visible effects were understood or completely described.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The record says eventual consistency may be delayed but omits duplicate charges visible to users. All fields pass while the substantive trade-off is missing.

controls.reason: A versioned financial-calculation contract can explicitly define all seven named calculation policies as exact modes, scales, timings, and allocation rules.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried omitting residual handling, leaving rounding mode implicit, and binding tax timing to another version; exact field and revision checks reject each. Legal correctness is not asserted.

controls.reason: Inclusive versus exclusive bounds can be represented by exact endpoint flags in authoritative schemas and policies, making definition fully decidable.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an unlabeled endpoint, contradictory flags, and prose using only `limit`; schema validation rejects each. Whether the chosen bound is appropriate is outside the rule.

controls.reason: Each declared limit can use a closed scope enum for request, user, tenant, account, window, region, or global, making its scope definition exact.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a numeric limit without scope, a time-window limit without window duration, and two conflicting scopes; structured validation rejects each.

controls.reason: An approximate-algorithm inventory is not independently complete, and accepted error bounds require accountable product or safety judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An approximate deduplication routine is omitted, while every registered approximation has a documented approved bound. The proposal passes despite the hidden algorithm.

controls.reason: Records do not prove runtime storage uses an unambiguous scale, and deciding when original zone or offset carries business meaning is contextual.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A recurring appointment stores only UTC despite local-zone business meaning, while the schema record marks zone not required. Required fields pass but future behavior shifts.

controls.reason: Whether local civil-time rules matter is a domain decision, and a declared temporal-field inventory can omit fixed-offset uses.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A payroll cutoff uses `+01:00` and is labelled instant-only, while listed civil fields use IANA zones. The proposal passes despite local rule changes.

controls.reason: Type names or documentation fields do not prove code semantically distinguishes eight temporal concepts across conversions, storage, and APIs.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The same integer type represents a duration and an instant but records label them separately. The structured contract passes while implementation still conflates them.

controls.reason: Applicability depends on judging when wall-clock adjustment is unsafe, and source scans cannot prove all elapsed-time and deadline paths use monotonic clocks.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A lease timeout uses wall time but is excluded as safe; declared timer calls use monotonic APIs. The proposal passes while clock rollback extends the lease.

controls.reason: Tokens, leases, caches, signatures, and coordination are five explicit categories whose numeric clock-skew tolerances can be defined in a versioned contract.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a category with no tolerance, a nonnumeric `reasonable` value, and conflicting versions; exact category and policy checks reject each. Enforcement is not claimed.

controls.reason: Whether interoperability requires a standard timestamp format is contextual, and a format record does not prove every external serialization uses it.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An external partner feed emits locale-formatted time but is labelled internal and omitted. All declared interoperable fields specify RFC 3339, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Determining when offset alone cannot preserve future civil meaning requires domain interpretation, while temporal-field inventories can omit schedules.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A future appointment stores only an offset but is classified as an instant; all declared recurring fields include zone IDs. The proposal passes.

controls.reason: Deadline contracts can encode exact inclusive or exclusive semantics and a named cutoff zone, so the two required definitions are fully checkable.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a deadline with no boundary flag, a local cutoff without zone, and conflicting fields; schema validation rejects each. Runtime correctness is a separate rule.

controls.reason: Recurring-job inventories and source patterns cannot prove correct behavior for all missed, repeated, and overlapping runs under distributed scheduling and failures.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Two workers overlap after a lease partition even though the local scheduler has all three handlers. Declared source checks pass while the job does not handle overlap safely.

controls.reason: A source analyzer cannot enumerate every machine timestamp parser or track locale influence through wrappers, reflection, generated code, and libraries.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A wrapper obtains the user's locale and passes it indirectly to a protocol parser; the forbidden direct-call pattern is absent, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: When a timestamp is submitted as evidence, its authenticated evidence record can require exact source, precision, and uncertainty fields.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a timestamp without source, precision expressed ambiguously, and uncertainty from another sample; schema and evidence-ID joins reject each. Timestamp truth is separate.

controls.reason: The rule bundles documentation with the semantic decision about when Unicode distinctions matter; a record can omit contexts or approve blind normalization incorrectly.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A signature input normalizes two distinct identifiers but is labelled search text, while every registered context has a form. The proposal passes despite losing a required distinction.

controls.reason: Documentation labels do not prove algorithms use the correct byte, code-unit, code-point, or grapheme length for each semantic operation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A UI limit uses UTF-16 units where graphemes are required, while a contract lists all four concepts. Record validation passes despite conflated runtime behavior.

controls.reason: Universal absence of locale-sensitive transformations on all machine and security fields cannot be proven from incomplete field and call inventories.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unlisted token canonicalizer uses Turkish lowercase through a wrapper. Direct calls on declared fields are clean, so the source check passes.

controls.reason: `Where applicable` requires locale-domain judgment, and dependency or configuration records do not prove runtime locale behavior uses correct BCP 47 and CLDR semantics.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A custom locale parser rejects a valid tag but is omitted as nonapplicable; declared tags and CLDR versions pass record checks.

controls.reason: The phrase `other identifiers` leaves scope open, and identity comparison rules require domain-specific semantics that cannot be completed by five headings.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Usernames and emails have rules, but an account alias identifier is omitted and compared with unsafe locale folding. The record passes while canonical rules are incomplete.

controls.reason: Boundary and parser inventories are incomplete, and source syntax does not prove malformed sequences are validated before every semantic use.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A generated CSV importer accepts malformed UTF-8 before replacement policy runs; it is absent from the declared boundary set. Listed parsers pass.

controls.reason: Limit records neither prove enforcement nor completeness across every parser, decompressor, reference resolver, and processing path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A library parser performs unbounded entity expansion through an unlisted code path, while registered parsers have all seven numeric fields. The proposal passes.

controls.reason: Parser and protocol inventories can omit consumers, and nonempty fields need not define exact outcomes for seven malformed-input classes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A legacy YAML parser has undefined duplicate-key behavior but is absent; listed contracts say `handle` for every field. The proposal passes.

controls.reason: A shared schema record does not prove producer and consumer implementations agree on semantics, units, defaults, nullability, and compatibility at runtime.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Both sides reference version 2, but the producer emits milliseconds and the consumer interprets seconds. Record identifiers match while semantics disagree.

controls.reason: Source patterns cannot enumerate every byte-identity dependency or prove serializers are canonical across maps, numbers, Unicode, versions, and libraries.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A cache key uses nondeterministic map serialization in an unlisted wrapper. Registered signature serializers are canonical, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Proving absence of JSON ordering and excess-precision assumptions across all languages, libraries, generated code, and indirect comparisons is unbounded.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A generated client relies on insertion order but is excluded from the scan; all declared consumers match the numeric profile. The proposal passes.

controls.reason: Whether an operation failed and whether success was returned merely for client simplicity are semantic and intent questions, not source-pattern facts.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An endpoint returns 200 with `{ok:false}` for a failed update because the team calls it a transport success. Syntax passes while reviewers can disagree about the prohibited behavior.

controls.reason: Safety, idempotency, cacheability, and accuracy are behavioral properties across all effects and retries, not annotations or local syntax.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An endpoint is marked idempotent but sends duplicate email on replay through an omitted side effect. Metadata passes while operation semantics are inaccurate.

controls.reason: Endpoint and response inventories can omit routes, and `where relevant` leaves content-sniffing applicability undefined across clients and formats.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A legacy upload response lacks nosniff and encoding but is absent from the inventory. Declared routes set headers correctly, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Static checks cannot prove media-type validation dominates parser selection through all aliases, negotiation branches, dynamic dispatch, and generated clients.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A fallback path selects a parser before checking the media type, hidden behind a wrapper the analyzer treats as validated. Declared paths pass.

controls.reason: `Forward-compatible` and `bounded` protocol extension behavior require future-version assumptions, resource thresholds, and behavioral oracles absent from record fields.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unknown extension triggers recursive fallback for a future peer, while the contract merely says `ignore extensions`. The record passes despite unbounded incompatible behavior.

controls.reason: Externally consumed format and API inventories can omit shadow, partner, generated, or undocumented interfaces, allowing them to evade versioning and deprecation policy.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A partner CSV feed is absent from the registry and changes without versioning. Every registered external API has both policies, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Static numeric limits do not prove actual resource consumption remains bounded across composition, failures, inputs, concurrency, libraries, and operating systems.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Each local buffer is capped, but an unbounded number of capped buffers exhausts memory. All source-level limit checks pass while total consumption is unbounded.

controls.reason: The memory-unsafe-code inventory can omit code, and roadmap plus defense records do not prove compiler, runtime, sandbox, fuzzing, and isolation defenses are effective.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unsafe native plugin is unregistered; another component lists six defenses but runs outside the sandbox. Structured fields pass while protection is incomplete.

controls.reason: Temporary-file creation can occur through wrappers, libraries, shell commands, generated code, and platform APIs outside a complete static call inventory.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unlisted helper creates a predictable world-readable file, while every direct standard-library call uses secure flags. The source check passes.

controls.reason: Child-process inventories and source configurations cannot prove effective limits across shells, wrappers, libraries, platforms, inherited state, and runtime overrides.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A wrapper inherits a production credential and has no output cap but is omitted from the spawn inventory. Direct process calls satisfy all six limits, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Security-relevant outcomes and unnecessary personal data require security and privacy judgment, while source syntax cannot determine runtime log values across all paths.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A debug formatter logs reset tokens and optional profile data through an unlisted sink. Declared security events are logged safely, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: A weakness register cannot prove all code weaknesses or threat findings are discovered, and correct CWE applicability requires security expertise.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A race-condition weakness is absent from the findings set; every listed issue maps to a CWE and threat row. The proposal passes despite an unmapped weakness.

controls.reason: Selecting input-controlled or high-volume operations and validating time and space complexity analysis require semantic algorithm and workload judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A quadratic report builder is labelled low-volume and omitted; listed operations contain complexity strings. The proposal passes while a high-volume operation is unanalyzed.

controls.reason: Which invariants are performance-sensitive and whether benchmark methodology is complete and valid require contextual performance judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A benchmark document lists environment and command but omits cache state and workload distribution for a sensitive path. Required headings pass while methodology is inadequate.

controls.reason: Recorded variance, warmup, sample size, and environment do not establish stability without a defined statistical protocol and acceptance threshold.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A three-sample noisy benchmark records all four fields and is labelled stable. The schema passes although repeated results vary by 80 percent.

controls.reason: A performance report or gate can deterministically require at least one approved latency percentile and a tail metric in addition to any average.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an average-only report, a percentile without tail window, and metrics from another revision; exact metric-type and binding checks reject each. Representativeness is not claimed.

controls.reason: Background-work bounds and yielding to critical operations are runtime scheduling properties over incomplete job inventories, while criticality needs product judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unlisted indexer holds the main thread during checkout; declared jobs have numeric caps and yield points. The source contract passes while critical work is starved.

controls.reason: Repository configuration cannot prove monitoring is active or complete across releases, metrics, environments, and resource dimensions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A production memory-growth metric is omitted and the dashboard is disabled after deployment. Source files still contain monitoring rules, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Security-sensitive randomness applicability and cryptographic suitability require security judgment, while source scans cannot enumerate every random source and environment path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A session token uses a deterministic library RNG through a wrapper omitted from the inventory; declared production RNG calls are secure. The proposal passes.

controls.reason: A controlled-clock provider record cannot prove every time-dependent component, library, static call, and generated path is controllable in tests.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A retry helper reads the system clock directly but is absent from the time-behavior inventory. Declared modules inject clocks, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Observable-outcome inventories cannot enumerate every state transition, retry, reconciliation, queue, and partial-failure path or prove signals remain available at runtime.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unlisted reconciliation failure emits no metric or event, while every declared outcome has telemetry. The source check passes despite an opaque failure.
